facts.label: Conselho e obrigação
facts.sub: Use should + verbo base para conselho: You should read the guide. Use have to / has to + verbo base para obrigação: I have to leave at five.

facts.label: Should
facts.sub: Use should + verbo base para dar conselho: You should draw it on the computer. You should start now. Should não leva s e não leva to. É o jeito simples e amigável de sugerir algo.

facts.label: Have to
facts.sub: Use have to + verbo base para falar de algo necessário: I have to leave at five. Com he, she e it, use has to: He has to wait. Em inglês simples, é muito comum.

pages.title: A small office · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Monday morning in a small office in Halifax. A new machine sits on the big table. Frank puts a roll of white plastic inside. The screen shows a green light. His coworker Rui walks in. He looks at the new printer.
“Hi, Rui! The new 3D printer is ready.” says Frank. “Great! I want to print a small phone stand.” says Rui. “Nice idea. First, you should draw it on the computer.” says Frank.
